items.title: Welfare of child can't be sole reason to order paternity test: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently held that trial courts cannot order paternity tests by merely stating that the welfare of the child in question is paramount [Filix Miller and Felix Miller v. xxx] . Justice Lalitha Kanneganti said that the trial court did not provide sufficient reasoning as to why hard scientific evidence was needed, as mandated by the Supreme Court in Ivan Rathinam v. Milan Joseph . "The trial Court has not addressed the petitioner's constitutional objection through this balancing exercise. Merely observing that the welfare of the child is paramount does not answer whether the proposed examination is necessary and proportionate." Justice Lalitha kanneganti The High Court thus set aside a family court order that directed a man to undergo a DNA test in order to determine whether he was the biological father of a child in a maintenance petition filed by the child. The minor child had filed the petition for maintenance and was represented through his mother. During the pendency of the case, the mother filed an interim application seeking a DNA test in order to determine paternity, since the father denied having fathered the child. The family court directed the minor and the father to provide their blood samples in order to determine paternity. The father appealed the decision before the High Court, stating an earlier civil court order had rejected the mother's application seeking a DNA test. He argued that the family court directing the same would be an abuse of the process of law. Counsel appearing for the minor child and mother argued the child had a right to know her biological parentage as an integral part of her right to dignity, identity and personal liberty under Article 21 of the Constitution. He contended that the previous rejection did not amount to a bar to seek the test out in another case. After noting the father's admission that he had had physical relations with the mother, the High Court said that a DNA examination could not be ordered by the lower court when sufficient evidence was already available. Outlining the fine balance between the privacy and bodily autonomy of the father and the child's welfare, the Court said that rejecting the test did not entail alleging that the biological relationship between the father and son did not exist. Delhi High Court Justice Tejas Karia will deliver the keynote address at the event. The summit will feature discussions involving senior lawyers, law firm partners, arbitration practitioners and international legal professionals. Pallavi Shroff , Managing Partner at Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co, will deliver a keynote presentation at a session titled Associate to rainmaker – what no one tells you about becoming partner . items.title: Prompt, proofread, publish: A practitioners' guide to using AI for legal drafting and content
items.summary: After the Pooja Ramesh Singh judgment debacle , the question is no longer whether lawyers should use generative AI. It is how to use it judiciously so every outcome survives a judge, a client and a bar council. This traces back to July 2, 2026, when a Supreme Court bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe set aside NCLT and NCLAT orders in Pooja Ramesh Singh v. Jammu and Kashmir Bank Ltd because they rested on precedents that didn’t even exist in real life. The Court called this out, stating zero tolerance for unverified, hallucinated AI-generated authorities and characterising their citation as misconduct by any advocate. The Court then directed the Bar Council of India to constitute a committee to address the problem. It wasn’t an isolated incident that led the Supreme Court to take a strong stand against AI-generated content. A month earlier, the Supreme Court’s AI committee released the draft Regulations for Use of Artificial Intelligence in Courts, 2026, which require lawyers to disclose AI assistance in pleadings and filings. Together, these developments raise a practical question. This piece explains how these tools actually work, where they genuinely help with drafting and legal content, and a working method that keeps advocates (not the model) in control of the outcome. What is the machine actually doing? You need to understand that a large language model doesn't look anything up. It predicts the most probable next word, given its context, based on patterns it learned from its training data. This is how it writes fluent prose and why it can also produce a perfectly formatted, entirely fictional citation. Everyone needs to distinguish between the two sources of an AI model's responses. The first is parametric memory. This is what the model absorbed in training, which stops at a fixed cutoff and is thin on Indian case law compared with American and English material. The second is the context window. It’s the text you place in front of the model in that conversation, such as a judgment, a statute or even a term sheet draft, followed by a prompt. There is also a real difference between a general-purpose chatbot - as we’re seeing with models like Claude, Perplexity, ChatGPT, Gemini, etc - and India-specific research products such as SCC Online’s AI Tools, Manupatra’s assistant or CaseMine’s AMICUS. items.summary: The family of Jayabalakrishnan, the victim in the Mercedes-Benz car crash case, has moved the Kerala High Court seeking the cancellation of bail granted in the matter to the 17-year-old teenager who had driven the car. Jayabalakrishnan's family has challenged a recent sessions court order refusing to cancel the grant of bail to the minor. Justice C Jayachandran today issued notice and sought the State's response in the matter. The case will be heard further next week. Justice C Jayachandran The accused teenager was driving a Mercedes-Benz car when he hit a two-wheeler in Kochi's Cheranalloor in the early hours of October 25, killing its rider, Jayabalakrishnan. The case drew more attention after it came to light that the youth was the son of a sitting additional district judge. The teenager was initially booked for the offences of rash driving and causing death by negligence under Sections 281 and 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS). After continued protests by the victim's family and local residents, the police added more serious offences punishable under Section 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) BNS read with Sections 181, 183, 199A(1) and 199A(2) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (MVA). A Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) granted the accused teenager bail on October 26. Last week, Ernakulam Additional District and Sessions Judge Kavitha Gangadharan dismissed appeals filed by the State and Jayabalakrishnan's relatives against the JJB's decision. The Additional Sessions Court opined that there were no circumstances warranting denial of bail to the Child in Conflict with Law (CCL) in this case. Moreover, Judge Gangadharan also flagged several issues in the manner in which the case was handled right from the beginning by the police, the Juvenile Justice Board, the State prosecution, and the family of the deceased. Among other observations, the Additional Sessions Court also questioned why an FIR was lodged in this case since the offences alleged against the CCL did not fall under the category of "heinous" crimes. It opined that this was not a case where an FIR should have been filed, as there are child-sensitive methods of investigation prescribed under the law in cases involving a CCL. items.title: The ‘right to nominate’ under DPDP: A statutory right with no statutory procedure
items.summary: As more of a person’s life moves online, a need has emerged to address what happens when an individual dies or is unable to access their digital data due to incapacity. India’s new data protection law attempts to address this through the nomination right but leaves gaps that a data fiduciary must fill to comply with the legislation's objectives. Section 14(1) of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (“ DP Act ”) allows an individual, the data principal, to nominate any other person who may, on the data principal’s death or incapacity, exercise that individual’s statutory rights under the DP Act and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (“ DP Rules ”). The Act grants the nominee broad authority to exercise powers as if stepping into the shoes of the data principal. Does the right to nominate fill the gap it was designed to fill? The gap the provision attempts to fill is genuine, but the machinery to operate it is thin. Further, because the law on whether digital personal data can be considered “property” capable of succession is still undeveloped, it can lead to conflict when an heir stakes a competing claim. Section 38, which provides that the DP Act prevails in the event of conflict with other laws, does not address the question related to succession or access rights of the heirs. Thus, this creates considerable ambiguity for all stakeholders. As the law stands, without legislative guidance, conflicts may arise between nominees and an individual's legal heirs. The Supreme Court confirmed in its December 2023 judgment in Shakti Yezdani v. Jayanand Jayant Salgaonkar that nomination under Indian law creates neither a statutory testament nor a third line of succession. Accordingly, where a nominee’s decision conflicts with the wishes of the legal heir, the courts will need to reconcile the data principal’s intentions, expressed through their nominee, with the legal heirs’ interests. A situation could arise where a nominee wishes to delete the data, but the heirs require retention for probate, tax, or litigation. Rule 14(4) of the DP Rules permits the data principal to nominate “ one or more individuals ” but says nothing about whether multiple nominees act jointly or severally, how conflicting instructions should be resolved, or what happens if a nominee dies before the data principal. items.summary: A Kerala court has issued notice to former Kerala Director General of Police, R Sreelekha, on a private complaint concerning her remarks against Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi. [KP Sreekumar v R Sreelekha] Judicial First Class Magistrate at Mavelikara Soorya S Sukumaran issued notice on November 10 on a complaint filed by Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee General Secretary KP Sreekumar alleging criminal defamation. The Court listed the matter for further consideration on December 2. Sreekumar filed the complaint on October 20, alleging criminal defamation under Section 356(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The provision covers publishing or making an allegation about a person with the intention, knowledge or reason to believe that it will harm their reputation, subject to statutory exceptions. The complaint stemmed from Sreelekha's speech delivered at a Bharatiya Janta Party (BJP) gathering in Punalur on October 14, where she allegedly linked Gandhi's conduct during the protests in Delhi to excessive drug consumption. " That by making the aforesaid statement, the Accused falsely and maliciously alleged that Shri Rahul Gandhi's behavior during a democratic protest in Delhi resembled that of a person acting under the severe influence of drugs and narcotics, " the complaint stated. She delivered the speech at a meeting organised by BJP's Kollam East District committee in support of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar. items.title: Aadhaar card not conclusive proof of age; postmortem report more reliable: Madhya Pradesh High Court
items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court recently held that an Aadhaar card cannot be treated as conclusive proof of a person's age, observing that that a postmortem report is a more reliable indicator [ Rajesh Singh & Anr. v Rahul Singh & Ors. ]. Justice Amit Seth made the observation while enhancing the compensation awarded to the parents of a 13-year-old boy who died in a motor accident in December 2019. A Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal had earlier relied on the boy's Aadhaar card to determine his age to be 14 years old. The insurance company, on the other hand, pointed to the postmortem report which recorded him as 13 years old. The Court found merit in the insurance company's argument and observed that an Aadhaar card cannot, by itself, establish the age of its holder conclusively. "An Aadhaar Card is primarily an identity document and cannot, by itself, be treated as conclusive proof of the age of its holder. On the other hand, the age recorded in the postmortem report is based upon medical assessment conducted in the course of postmortem examination," said the Court. The Court held that the medical assessment in the postmortem report was a more reliable basis for determining the deceased's age. "In the facts and circumstances of the present case, this Court finds the medical opinion recorded in the postmortem report to be a more reliable basis for determining the age of the deceased," held the Court. Justice Amit Seth The Court was hearing an appeal filed by the boy's parents. They sought enhancement of the ₹5.45 lakh compensation awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT), Bhind, in September 2022. The tribunal had determined the boy's age as 14 years, 7 months and 9 days on the basis of his Aadhaar card. However, the insurance company challenged this finding, pointing out that the postmortem report recorded his age as 13 years. The Court also considered the multiplier to be applied while calculating compensation. The insurance company argued that a multiplier of 15, instead of 18, should apply since the boy was below 15 years of age. The parents opposed this, relying on a 2025 Supreme Court judgment in Ku Aarti v. items.title: Centre to launch ‘evening courts' on pilot basis in Delhi, Bihar, Andhra to tackle case pendency
items.summary: The Union government is set to establish ‘evening courts’ as a pilot project in Delhi, Bihar and Andhra Pradesh to tackle case pendency. The same was revealed by Union Minister of State for Law and Justice (Independent Charge) Arjun Ram Meghwal in an interview with The New Indian Express. In the interview, the Meghwal outlined the government's strategy to expedite case disposal. Under the proposed arrangement, courts currently operating during standard daytime hours, will extend their sittings into the evening for a few additional hours specifically to hear and clear pending matters. The minister further said that the Centre plans to engage the services of retired judges to preside over the evening sessions. The initiative is slated to commence shortly in collaboration with the respective High Courts. The minister explained that following a comprehensive performance assessment of the pilot phase in the initial three regions, the Central government will consider expanding the model to other States and Union Territories. Beyond the introduction of evening courts, the Union Minister highlighted the government's continued reliance on alternative mechanisms to ease the institutional burden on courts. In this regard, he highlighted an increased focus on resolving and disposing of matters through Lok Adalats and Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) frameworks. items.title: Delhi High grants interim relief to Singapore law firm in tax dispute
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently restrained the Income Tax Department from taking coercive steps to recover tax from international law firm Holman Fenwick Willan Singapore LLP pursuant to an assessment order passed against the firm in 2025. A Division Bench of Justices Dinesh Mehta and Aditi Choudhary passed the order after the law firm submitted that it had no presence in India, yet the Income Tax Department had allotted it a Permanent Account Number (PAN) without any application. "The respondents shall not take any coercive measure for recovery of the demand raised by assessment order dated 09.05.2025 and consequential demand notice dated 24.12.2025 issued to the petitioner ," the Court said. The Court passed the order on October 16 after the law firm challenged an assessment order dated May 9, 2025, a penalty order dated December 24, 2025, and the consequential demand notice issued on the same date. Appearing for the firm, advocate Vibhooti Malhotra submitted that Holman Fenwick Willan Singapore LLP was a maritime law firm with no presence in India and had never applied for a PAN. She alleged that the Income Tax Department had nevertheless allotted a PAN to the firm and proceeded to assess its income without its knowledge. After hearing the submissions, the Court granted interim relief to the firm and directed Senior Standing Counsel Puneet Rai, appearing for the Income Tax Department, to obtain instructions and file a short counter-affidavit within three weeks. The matter will be heard next on November 18. Advocates Bhuvnesh Satija and Aniket Khanduri also represented the law firm. Besides Rai, Junior Standing Counsel Ashwini Kumar and Rishabh Nangia also appeared for the Income Tax Department. items.title: Can banks financing AI data centres be held liable for water, energy impacts? What a BIICL report says
items.summary: Banks financing data centres and artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure in India could face environmental litigation over water and energy impacts, a report published by the British Institute of International and Comparative Law (BIICL) has suggested. The report, authored by Senior Advocate Shyam Divan and Advocates Ria Singh Sawhney, Sugandha Yadav and Shaishir Divatia, identified the sector’s expansion as a potential basis for claims concerning environmental harm associated with bank financing. “ Looking ahead, the rapid expansion of data centre and artificial intelligence infrastructure financing in India, which carries significant and increasingly well-documented local water and energy impacts, may in time provide the factual basis for the first concrete Bank Local Impact Claim brought in this jurisdiction, ” it stated. The report used the term “Bank Local Impact Claims” to describe cases or complaints against banks concerning local environmental damage caused by projects they financed. This was an analytical category developed for the study, not an established category of legal action in India. Such claims need not involve climate change and financing a harmful project would not, by itself, establish a bank’s liability. The authors reasoned that localised damage could be easier to establish causally than the indirect harm associated with emissions from activities financed by banks. Titled Banks and Climate Litigation: India Report , the study examined potential proceedings against banks and regulators through public interest litigation (PIL), the National Green Tribunal (NGT) and shareholder actions. It distinguished claims concerning climate change from those involving local environmental impacts of bank-financed projects. The latter need not have a climate-related dimension. The report identified a PIL against a private commercial bank, with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) joined as a respondent, as the most promising primary route. A strong case could involve financing a demonstrably harmful project while making misleading climate disclosures. Crucially, the proposed claim would concern the bank’s own failures to assess risks or comply with legal obligations. “ The cause of action proposed in this Report does not ask the court to hold the bank vicariously liable for the borrower’s pollution. One of the allegations made by the husband was that his wife was in an extra-marital relationship as she used to talk to an unknown male over mobile phone. “To our considered view, such allegations are typical gender-based stereotypes, where, if a woman talks to a man, even if he is a friend, charges of adultery or of an extramarital relationship are levelled. items.title: Transparency on trial: Mapping courts’ compliance with the RTI Act
items.summary: The effectiveness of the Right to Information (RTI) regime has, in recent years, come under a cloud of uncertainty with commentators pointing at a progressive weakening of RTI mechanisms. Among the concerns are onerous delays in appointments of information commissioners and other officials, rising backlogs and arbitrary rejections of requests by public authorities . The amendment effected to Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act by the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 further exacerbated these concerns as it empowered public authorities to deny information if it qualified as ‘personal information’, without requiring it to be weighed against public interest. While the High Courts and the Supreme Court often find themselves adjudicating upon the failure of government ministries and departments to comply with the RTI Act, the courts themselves are guilty of not adhering to the principles of the Act. The 2024-25 Annual Report of the Central Information Commission (CIC) reveals that among all public authorities in the country, the Delhi High Court has the highest rate of rejection of RTI applications followed by the Supreme Court. More often than not, courts withhold information that relates to institutional probity and conduct of judicial personnel -information that is crucial for affixing accountability. Hence, it is imperative to analyse these acts of omission and commission. Weaponising exemptions Firstly, courts have been thwarting RTI queries seeking clarity on judicial examinations, disciplinary conduct of judges and internal administrative affairs, by taking the cover of the exemptions laid out under Section 8 of the Act, even where the information demanded lies beyond the ambit of the exemptions. Particularly, Section 8(1)(j) is often invoked by High Courts, thus lending credence to the apprehensions being expressed over the DPDP amendment. In a similar case, the Delhi High Court in August last year had refused to disclose complaints details, again primarily invoking Section 8(1)(j). items.title: Former YSRCP MP Vijayasai Reddy launches new party in Andhra Pradesh
items.summary: Former YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) MP V Vijayasai Reddy has returned to politics, launching the Parivarthana Rajaneethi Party (PRP) on Wednesday, November 11 at the A Convention Centre in Vijayawada. He said the party would challenge the dominance of two political families in Andhra Pradesh and create opportunities for younger leaders. Unveiling its white and saffron flag, featuring a Dharma Chakra at the centre, Vijayasai said the organisation would offer an alternative to the ruling Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and the Opposition YSRCP. Addressing the gathering, he said political leadership in the state should not remain confined to two families. He questioned why the Chief Minister, ministers and MLAs should come only from these families, referring to Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu and YSRCP president YS Jagan Mohan Reddy. He said people should have the freedom to question all political leaders, including himself, over wrongdoing. Vijayasai said the party would focus on identifying and nurturing young leaders rather than creating another individual political figure. He said he wanted a capable young person to become Chief Minister, regardless of caste or family background. Leadership, he argued, should be earned through public support and merit rather than inherited. Referring to Shiv Sena founder Bal Thackeray and Bahujan Samaj Party founder Kanshi Ram, he said he intended to play the role of a margadarshi, or mentor, while younger leaders took on political and organisational responsibilities. He said the party would work towards building grassroots leadership and giving representation to different caste and social groups. He also said the PRP would prioritise the welfare of weaker sections and focus on agricultural development, employment for young people, affordable education and improving living standards for poor and middle-class families. He described the party as a platform for Gen Z leadership and said it would contest all 175 Assembly constituencies in Andhra Pradesh. Vijayasai said the party's doors would remain open to those willing to join its political journey. He also announced that he would raise with Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy the removal of 26 castes from the Backward Classes list in Telangana. The launch marks a return to active politics for Vijayasai, who resigned from the Rajya Sabha and announced his retirement from politics in January 2025. items.title: Telangana to scrap intermediate colleges, bring class 11 and 12 under schools
items.summary: The Telangana government has announced that it will introduce a 10+2 grade education system in schools from the next academic year, effectively replacing the current system of treating the two years after matriculation as a separate ‘intermediate’ system. School education will be split into three main levels – primary (nursery to class 4), secondary education (classes 5 to 8), and senior secondary education (classes 9 to 12) – Chief Minister Revanth Reddy said on November 11 following a review meeting of the education department. Revanth Reddy also handles the education portfolio. The CM said that under the new system, students must be trained to have a command over language and communication skills by the time they complete class 12. He expressed concern over students discontinuing their education after class 10, with dropouts consisting predominantly of girls, and children from Dalit, tribal, and minority communities. He noted that dropout rates are significantly lower in government-run institutions such as Kendriya Vidyalayas, Navodaya Vidyalayas, and Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas, which offer continuous education up to class 12. So far, students enrolled in Telangana state board schools studied for the intermediate in junior colleges overseen by the Telangana State Board of Intermediate Education. These junior colleges, mainly run by a few private institutions in the Telugu states, usually have integrated coaching classes for engineering and medical entrance tests as their primary focus. They have come under criticism for years for placing excessive academic pressure on students. The CM also assured that the employment and retirement benefits of lecturers and non-teaching staff in junior colleges would remain unaffected. CM Revanth Reddy instructed officials to move government-run welfare hostels or residential schools out from rented buildings, and to construct hostels and residential schools equipped with full-fledged facilities. He also asked to ensure adequate toilets and water supply in all such government residential schools. He also directed officials to accelerate the recruitment process for Assistant Professors, Associate Professors, and other faculty positions in state universities.

items.title: CM Vijay meets TVK MLAs, asks them to focus on public grievances
items.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has warned two Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) legislators facing allegations of misconduct that action could follow if their conduct damages the party’s reputation. He also asked all party MLAs to avoid controversies and concentrate on public grievances. CM Vijay held a nearly three-hour meeting with TVK legislators at a resort near Mamallapuram in Chengalpattu district on Wednesday, November 11. The meeting was held six months after the party formed the government, following a series of controversies involving its elected representatives. The two legislators who CM Vijay met separately were Thuraiyur MLA and Deputy Speaker Ravishankar and Kallakurichi MLA Arul Vignesh. Ravishankar was recently filmed assaulting a person who had approached him with a complaint. Vignesh is accused of inappropriate behaviour towards Kallakurichi District Collector Padmaja. Sources told TNM that CM Vijay reprimanded both legislators and cautioned them that the party would take action if they brought disrepute to the government or TVK. The Chief Minister also met the other legislators in groups of 10. An MLA told TNM that CM Vijay exchanged Deepavali greetings with them and gave them gifts. He asked them to focus on their constituencies, address public complaints, and prioritise issues affecting residents. Another MLA said several legislators raised difficulties they had faced while dealing with government officials. CM Vijay listened to their feedback, noted their grievances, and assured them that he would look into the issues. He also urged the MLAs to remain vigilant and not get drawn into unnecessary controversies that could affect the public image of the party and the government. The legislators had first met TVK general secretary and ministers N Anand, Aadhav Arjuna and CTR Nirmal Kumar. A source said they were cautioned against getting involved in controversies even before their interaction with the Chief Minister. The meeting was held at a private resort rather than the party office, after MLAs were initially asked to assemble in Chennai. The venue was confirmed later, prompting speculation on social media that the legislators had been moved to a resort amid fears of defections. Most TVK MLAs attended the meeting, while a few were absent.

items.title: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng says stopped from traveling to Hyderabad on MHA orders
items.summary: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng Svendsen has alleged that she was stopped from travelling to India at the last minute, despite having political clearance and a visa, based on orders from the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). Helle was invited to speak at the Bharat Summit conference organised by the Congress in Hyderabad on November 14, at a panel discussion on ‘The Future of Media’. Helle became a recognised face in India after she confronted Prime Minister Narendra Modi for not taking questions from the media during his visit to the Norwegian capital Oslo on May 18. She has since frequently criticised PM Modi’s governance, and has asked questions about human rights violations and curbs on press freedom in his regime. On November 11, Helle said in an X post that she received a call from the Indian Embassy minutes before she left for the airport to catch her flight to India, saying she wouldn’t be allowed to enter the country due to orders from the MHA. Helle told TNM that the Embassy officials asked her to visit their office and physically have her visa revoked, which she refused to do. “I asked for a written explanation, but have not received it,” she said. Sources involved in organising the event also said that officials in both the Embassy and the Ministry of External Affairs said that they have no role in the matter, and that the orders came directly from the MHA. The sources said that the Bharat Summit has been organised in compliance with the MEA’s rules for international conferences, which says that additional clearance from MHA is required to grant a conference visa only when participants are “from Afghanistan, Pakistan, Iraq, Sudan, foreigners of Pakistani origin, and Stateless persons”, or if they are required to visit certain restricted or protected areas in India including Jammu and Kashmir and some northeastern states. Nearly 120 foreign nationals who had confirmed to attend the event were unable to travel as their visas were either delayed or rejected, the source said, adding that some of these invitees were questioned by Indian Embassy officials about their social media posts critical of the Modi government. In her X post, Helle addressed Union Home Minister Amit Shah and said she was confused about being denied entry to India. “I have political clearance. I have a visa. items.title: Karnataka moves Supreme Court to restore enhanced SC/ST quota struck down by HC
items.summary: The Karnataka government has approached the Supreme Court challenging a High Court verdict that struck down the enhanced reservation for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST). The state is seeking to restore the enhanced reservation, which took the total reservation in Karnataka from 50% to 56%. The government filed a Special Leave Petition (SLP) against the Karnataka High Court’s October 12 judgement, which held the enhancement to be constitutionally impermissible. A Government Order dated October 27 approved the move, following a Cabinet decision on October 15, the Chief Minister’s Office said in a statement on Wednesday, November 11. The Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in Educational Institutions and of Appointments or Posts in the Services under the State) Act, 2022, increased the quota for SC from 15% to 17% and from 3% to 7% for ST. The 32% reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBC) remained unchanged, taking the total to 56%. The legislation was enacted by the former BJP government following recommendations from a commission headed by retired judge HN Nagamohan Das. The High Court struck down Sections 3 and 4 of the Act, holding that the state had not met mandatory requirements for consultation with the National Commissions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. It said letters sent to the commissions after the law was enacted did not fulfil this requirement. The Congress government has accused the previous BJP regime of failing to secure constitutional protection for the enhanced quota by including it in the Ninth Schedule. The Nagamohan Das Commission had recommended such protection, and then Law minister JC Madhuswamy had publicly said in October 2022 that the move would be taken forward, the state government said. Instead, the BJP government promulgated an ordinance and subsequently passed the legislation ahead of the 2023 Assembly elections, the Congress government alleged. It pointed out that on March 21, 2023, then Union minister of state for Social Justice and Empowerment A Narayanaswamy had told Parliament that the Union government had not received a proposal from Karnataka on Ninth Schedule inclusion. The state sent its proposal seven weeks before the Assembly elections, according to the government. items.title: ‘60 days of suspension, now you want an apology?': Kerala HC questions Kalady varsity
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Wednesday, November 11, questioned the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (SSUS) in Kalady over its insistence that suspended students submit an unconditional apology as a condition for revoking their suspension. The court observed that the students had already been suspended for 60 days and questioned whether the period of suspension wasn’t sufficient punishment, even assuming there had been misconduct. Justice PV Kunhikrishnan was hearing a petition filed by 16 students challenging their suspension pending disciplinary proceedings over an incident during a protest on the university campus on August 13. "I am not accepting what they have done, but they have suffered. They have been out for 60 days. Assume for argument that there is misconduct, isn't 60 days enough?" the judge said, as per LiveLaw . During the hearing, the judge questioned the University's position that the students should apologise before their suspension could be withdrawn. The court observed that the students had already suffered the consequences of being kept away from the institution for two months, apart from losing the opportunity to appear for their semester examinations. The judge clarified that the court was not endorsing the students' alleged conduct but said the University should consider the consequences they had faced. The court also indicated that it would proceed with hearing the matter if the University did not reconsider its position. It posted the case for Friday, November 13, for further consideration. The students approached the Kerala High Court seeking relief from the suspension and permission to write their examinations. They argued that the attendance shortage cited against them was a consequence of the University preventing them from entering the campus. On October 30, a single judge of the High Court provisionally permitted the students to appear for their examinations, subject to the final outcome of their pending petition challenging the suspension. The University challenged this order before a Division Bench. On November 3, the Division Bench, comprising Justices Anil K Narendran and Muralee Krishna S, set aside the single judge's interim direction. It held that the students had not established their eligibility to appear for the examinations under the applicable university regulations, including requirements relating to minimum attendance and internal assessment. items.title: Kerala Police use force to remove LPST protester Valarmathi, demolish protest shed
items.summary: Valarmathi, the secretary of the All Kerala Lower Primary School Teachers (LPST) Rankholders Association who was on an indefinite hunger strike in Thiruvananthapuram, was forcibly removed from the protest site on the night of Wednesday, November 11. The police also took down the protesters’ shed and removed the boards they had put up. The police used force to shift Valarmathi to the General Hospital, citing doctor’s concerns as her fast-until-death entered its 16th day. Visuals from the protest site showed Valarmathi lying on a makeshift bed in the protest shed while a doctor examined her, and a group of police officers told her that she was going to be shifted as per the doctor’s instructions. Even as Valarmathi refused to move, the police brought out a stretcher to shift her. Other visuals of the police action also showed women police officers carrying Valarmathi away on a stretcher. “Do not take me away, the government should take action,” Valarmathi could be heard saying. She also said, “My body hurts.” The police put her in an ambulance and took her away. After the police took Valarmathi despite her resistance, M Jayakrishnan, another rank holder, reportedly began a fast-until-death raising the same demands. Protesters and Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) workers set up another shed in front of the Secretariat soon after the demolition. The action came hours after the protesters were issued a notice by the Cantonment Police, asking them to remove their makeshift shed and boards on the footpath in front of the state Secretariat. They were reportedly accused of encroaching the footpath. The protesters refused to comply. “The cases registered against us, and the move to take down our sheds are simply aimed at sabotaging the protest,” Valarmathi was quoted as saying by The New Indian Express. The Lower Primary School Teachers (LPST) rankholders association has been holding months-long protests in the state, demanding appointments to schools based on the May 2025 rank list published by the Public Service Commission. They are also demanding that the teacher student ratio in the state be set at 1:25, lowered from the current 1:30.

items.title: Revanth Reddy inaugurates restored Thammidikunta Lake in Hyderabad
items.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Wednesday, November 11, inaugurated the restored Thammidikunta Lake in Hyderabad’s Madhapur, following the removal of encroachments and waste. He also said Phase I of the Musi River rejuvenation project would begin soon, seeking support for the government’s plans. The lake, restored by the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA), has been expanded to around 30 acres. More than 30,000 truckloads of silt, construction debris, plastic and other waste, including biomedical waste, were removed during the work. Its depth has increased from 0.6 metres to 4.6 metres, while its water storage capacity has risen eightfold to 370 million litres, according to HYDRAA Commissioner A V Ranganath. The restored lake has a 1.6-km walking track, an open gym, a children’s play area, landscaped gardens and seating facilities. HYDRAA also reconstructed three inlets and an outlet to improve rainwater flow and diverted sewage through a 1,200-mm pipeline to prevent wastewater from entering the lake. The agency said the work would improve water storage, groundwater recharge and flood resilience in the surrounding areas. Ranganath also cited a National Environmental Engineering Research Institute report which found that groundwater levels in nearby areas had risen by 4.5 metres. Addressing the gathering, Revanth Reddy said nearly half of the 1,372 lakes that once existed in Hyderabad had disappeared due to various reasons. He said encroachments had contributed to waterlogging in residential areas during heavy rains and described the restoration of water bodies as part of his vision for developing Hyderabad into a world-class city. The Chief Minister also praised actor Akkineni Nagarjuna for voluntarily handing over two acres of land to the government for the lake’s restoration. There seems to have been a reconciliation between the government and the actor as HYDRAA had demolished Nagarjuna’s N Convention Centre in August 2024 over alleged encroachments into the lake’s Full Tank Level (FTL) and buffer zone. Revanth Reddy said the restored lake would be developed as a tourism destination and cultural centre, with the government seeking to create a ‘lake economy’ around it. He also proposed planting a Jammi tree on the premises and holding Dussehra celebrations there.
